headline: A firmer rupiah and cheaper oil pull the front end down 5–7bp on auction day while the 10Y holds at 7.68%, and the flow signal slips back into sell-off (−0.64) as the Vice President signals he may resign
summary: The rally moved to the front end: PHEI's IGSYC 1Y fell 6.8bp to 6.793%, the 2Y 5.1bp to 7.007% and the 5Y 3.0bp to 7.416%, while the 10Y slipped only 0.4bp to 7.684% and 15–30Y were unchanged, so the curve bull-steepened (2s5s 41bp, 5s10s 27bp and 10s20s 2.9bp, the latter two the steepest of nine stored PHEI days). The 1M point fell 14bp to 6.22%, and the 1Y–5Y sector is now at the low end of the nine days stored. Benchmark FR0109 fell 12.3bp to 7.251% and is 8.8bp rich to the curve, while FR0108 barely moved (7.574%). Sukuk followed the curve (fitted PBS 5Y 1.9bp through IGSYC; PBS040 −6bp but still 15.6bp cheap), the retail fit held 11bp rich at 5Y, and corporate curves fell in step with IGSYC, leaving AAA 3Y at 49bp over.
drivers: Rupiah and oil fed a front-end rally

JISDOR fixed at 18,059 (−0.24%) and spot closed near 18,062 as the dollar eased and Brent fell to about $90 on a pause in US–Iran escalation; the 1Y–5Y fell 3–7bp and the 1M 14bp. Benchmark FR0109 led the bonds (−12.3bp), and SRBI-style short paper was already in demand last week, but who bought today is not disclosed, so domestic bank buying is a hypothesis.
Supply and politics capped the long end

DJPPR auctioned nine SUN series for an indicative Rp30tn, including a new 2047 bond (FR0113); results were not yet published when this was written (MNC expected Rp33–38tn of bids). 15–30Y IGSYC ended unchanged, consistent with a supply concession ahead of new 20Y paper. In the afternoon the palace confirmed Vice President Gibran told President Prabowo he intends to resign over court rulings on his school certificate; the JCI still closed 1.02% higher at 5,125.73 and the rupiah kept its gain, so the first market read was calm.

The daily Bond Flow Signal fell to −0.64 from −0.50 (Nov 9 restated from −0.49), so the sell-off episode that began Oct 7 is still open, 17 sessions and +51.6bp on the 10Y. The rupiah part turned bearish (z +0.61) mainly because its 20-session window now starts from a low Sep 29 print (USD/IDR +1.74%), not because the rupiah weakened; the JCI part (z −1.75) and 10Y trend (z +1.64) eased, and the 280bp spread part (z +1.43) is the bullish one.
US Treasuries: a small sell-off, ignored again

Monday's New York session lifted the US 10Y 2bp to 4.88% and the 2Y 5bp to 4.56% after a soft 3-year auction, with markets pricing about an 80% chance of a December Fed hike; at the 1-year daily beta of 0.34 that implied +0.7bp for INDOGBs, yet the 10Y fell 0.4bp, so Treasuries explain none of today's move. Over four weeks the INDOGB 10Y is up 51.5bp while the US 10Y is down 22bp (26-week weekly beta −0.21): about +4.7bp is the Treasury-linked part and +46.8bp residual, which is what the US move does not explain, not proof of domestic selling or political risk. The INDOGB − UST spread is 280bp, 96th percentile of 52 weeks, a nominal pick-up before currency risk.
data: Soft consumption and BI's own October estimate (+1.0% y/y) argue against hikes for growth reasons; BI's price-expectation index rose, though.
Better but below a year ago; no change to BI's rupiah-first reaction function.
Kept December Fed-hike odds near 80%; a hike would narrow BI's room.
Up despite intervention. My read, not a BI commitment: BI can keep smoothing the rupiah near 18,000–18,200 before it has to hike.
A beat led by government spending: no growth case for an early cut.
Non-resident SBN net buy Rp9.55tn; equity net sell Rp16.88tn
October's sell-off was a price move more than a foreign exit in bonds; a month's inflows do not rule out November outflows (Rp2.29tn sold in the first week).
Softer than expected: inflation does not force BI's hand; the rupiah does.
view: The rally keeps leaning on a steadier rupiah and cheaper oil, and today it showed up at the front end, which now looks rich with the 1Y down 7bp this week, while the long end is pinned by supply and, from here, by the political story around the Vice President; the tests are the auction result, US CPI (Nov 10), MSCI's review (read in Jakarta early Nov 12) and BI (Nov 17–18). The daily Bond Flow Signal is −0.64, back in sell-off, with the JCI (z −1.75), the 10Y trend (z +1.64) and, on a base effect, the rupiah (z +0.61) bearish and the 280bp Treasury spread, 39bp above its 130-day average (z +1.43), bullish; the Oct 7 episode is still open at +51.6bp. That record needs weighing: on the daily build since June 2022 the signal scores a Sharpe of 0.75 outright and 0.89 hedged against Treasuries, but sell-off calls were right only 51% of the time over the next 20 sessions (rally calls 58%; hedged 62% and 51%), and the average 10Y move after a sell-off call was −1.8bp; the weekly build scores 0.42 and 0.56, and the US-trend variants reach 0.73 and 0.78 on the weekly build but were chosen after the fact and are not live; all are in-sample back-tests. Treasuries explain only about 5bp of the 52bp four-week rise, so the trend rests on the residual, the rupiah, BI and MSCI. I stay neutral on the 10Y: my underweight rule needs both the signal below −0.5 and the 10Y above 7.75%, and only the first holds; I expect 7.55–7.80% over two weeks. On the curve, the FR0109 → PBS040 switch hit its stop and is closed; I would not chase the front end or 5Y here and prefer to wait for the auction concession to fade before adding duration.

buckets.name: Front end 1–2Y vs BI-Rate
buckets.why: The IGSYC 1Y fell 6.8bp to 6.793%, 104bp over the 5.75% BI-Rate, the lowest of nine stored days (11th percentile, average 112bp), and the 2Y 5.1bp to 7.007%. The 1M point dropped 14bp to 6.22% and the 3M (0.25Y) is 6.32%, below last Friday's 12-month SRBI at 6.67%. Previous call (add at 1Y 7.10%) still unfilled, now 31bp away; the 1Y is 4bp from the 6.75% no-chase line.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add 1–2Y only at 1Y 7.10% or after a BI hike with JISDOR below 18,000; below 6.75% the front end prices an easing BI has not signalled.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y (FR0109 / PBS040)
buckets.why: The IGSYC 5Y fell 3.0bp to 7.416%, the lowest of nine stored days (11th percentile, average 7.508%), 10.6bp lower this month; the 2s5s10s fly is 14bp, also the lowest stored (average 27bp). FR0109 fell 12.3bp to 7.251% (8.8bp rich) while PBS040 fell 6bp to 7.429% (15.6bp cheap), so the FR0109 → PBS040 switch, entered at 10bp, widened to 17.9bp and hit its 16bp stop: closed, about −8bp. The outright entry (FR0109 7.60–7.70%) was not filled.
buckets.call: No position. Outright: buy FR0109 at 7.60–7.70% after a BI hike or with JISDOR below 18,000; target 7.35%, stop 7.95%. No re-entry of the PBS040 switch until the gap stops widening.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The IGSYC 10Y slipped 0.4bp to 7.684%, 96th percentile of the past year (172 days, average 6.79%) and 4bp off the 7.724% high of Nov 4. The signal fell back to −0.64, but the underweight rule also needs the 10Y above 7.75%, so it is not triggered. FR0108 at 7.574% stays 10bp rich to the curve.
buckets.call: Neutral. Underweight if the signal stays below −0.5 and the 10Y closes above 7.75%; tactical long only above 7.85% (stop 8.05%) or once the signal is above 0 with JISDOR below 18,000.

buckets.name: 10s20s curve (FR0108 vs FR0107)
buckets.why: IGSYC 10s20s steepened to 2.9bp, the steepest of nine stored days (average 1.1bp), as the front end led and the 20Y held. The benchmark spread FR0107 − FR0108 narrowed back to 4.5bp from 10.2bp as FR0107 rallied 6.4bp, so the steepener re-entry at −5bp is still 9.5bp away.
buckets.call: Wait. Re-enter the FR0108/FR0107 steepener duration-weighted at −5bp or lower, target +5bp, stop −12bp; new FR0113 supply could cheapen the 20Y first.

buckets.name: PBS sukuk vs FR
buckets.stance: FR over PBS034 at the long end
buckets.why: The fitted PBS 5Y is 1.9bp through IGSYC (38th percentile of eight stored days, average −2.3bp) and the 10Y 1.0bp through; the fit rests on four series (level 0.1bp, slope −5.6bp), so confidence is limited. PBS034 was flat at 7.602% and stays 9.7bp rich, PBS038 rose 1.5bp to 7.730% (2bp cheap), PBS030 fell 5.3bp to 6.842%. The switch-back condition (PBS034 5bp cheap) is not met.
buckets.call: Hold FR over PBS034; switch back once PBS034 is 5bp cheap to the curve. PBS040 at 15.6bp cheap is value for buy-and-hold accounts, not a trade while the gap is widening.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AAA 3Y)
buckets.why: PHEI's AAA 3Y fell 4.4bp to 7.648%, 49.3bp over IGSYC, unchanged and near the tightest of eight stored days (25th percentile, average 51.0bp). AA (86bp), A (156bp) and BBB (235bp over AA, average 245bp) also moved one-for-one with IGSYC, which suggests the corporate curves were repriced off the government curve rather than traded. With eight days stored the meter is thin; the add level (AAA 3Y past 70bp) was not reached.
buckets.call: Hold AAA/AA; add only if AAA 3Y widens past 70bp. Avoid BBB until the rupiah and politics settle; tight spreads are not a reason to chase.

buckets.name: Retail SBN 5Y (ORI/SR)
buckets.why: The fitted retail curve is 10.8bp through IGSYC at 5Y (88th percentile of eight stored days, average −14.7bp) and 10.4bp over at 2Y; the fit uses 21 series with a steep 80bp slope, so it is partly a fit artefact. Secondary spreads run from 62bp rich (SR022T3) to 43bp cheap (ORI027T3); ORI026T6 is 7.534%, 30bp over IGSYC. ST017 (open to Dec 2) floors at 6.95% (2Y) and 7.05% (4Y), now near the IGSYC 2Y at 7.01% and below the 4Y at 7.29%.
buckets.call: For new money, FR0109 or PBS040 give daily liquidity; ST017 suits hold-to-maturity buyers who want BI-hike upside. Buy secondary retail only at the cheap end (ORI026T6, ~30bp over IGSYC).

watch: Next: SUN auction results incl. new FR0113 (Tue Nov 10, evening), US October CPI and the US 10Y auction (Tue Nov 10), MSCI's November review (Nov 11 CET, read in Jakarta 05:00 WIB Nov 12), US PPI (Fri Nov 13), then BI's board meeting (Nov 17–18); a formal VP resignation, a weak auction or JISDOR above 18,200 would keep the signal in sell-off, while a rupiah below 18,000 would push a BI hike out.
